stated_limitation: Using only this small ensemble, Bayesian population decoding (`pynapple.decode_bayes`) reconstructed the animal's held-out heading with a median absolute circular error of about 48 degrees, versus the roughly 90 degrees expected by chance

justification.dataset: DANDI:000056 is the canonical Peyrache ADn/PoS head-direction dataset in freely foraging mice, exactly the standard choice for this phenomenon.
justification.handling: Data streamed from S3 with remfile, head direction correctly computed as the LED-to-LED vector angle, untracked (-1,-1) frames dropped, and analysis restricted to the longest awake foraging epoch.
justification.analysis: Circular statistics (Rayleigh vector), split-half reliability, and held-out Bayesian decoding are all appropriate and correct, but no shuffle/Rayleigh-significance null is provided for the tuning claim, relying instead on hard thresholds.
justification.correctness: The median 48 deg vs 90 deg chance reproduces from the code and matches the figure and is internally consistent, though the decoding ensemble is only 3 cells and no confidence interval is reported.
justification.figures: The polar tuning grid, criterion scatter, and decoding panels clearly show the effect with the HD cells highlighted, but the polar radial axes lack firing-rate units (cosmetic).
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate to the clean, strong result and it flags the small ensemble, though there is no dedicated limitations discussion of the low HD-cell yield or single session.
justification.verdict: A clean, reproducible demonstration of head-direction cells with correct methods and honest reporting that a rotation student could hand in with only minor additions requested.
